why: App.jsx holds query in useState and passes it to <BreedList query={query} />, and it hands setQuery to SearchBox as onQueryChange, but SearchBox.jsx keeps its own const [query, setQuery] = useState('') and its input updates only that local copy, never calling onQueryChange. Typing in the box never reaches App, so BreedList's query stays '' and the list never filters: the two children do not share one query.

step.title: Hold the query in App
step.instructions: In src/App.jsx, keep query in useState and pass it down: <SearchBox query={query} onQueryChange={setQuery} /> and <BreedList query={query} />. In src/SearchBox.jsx, the input reads value={query} and calls onQueryChange(e.target.value).

checks.label: App holds the query in state

hints: Only one component should own query; the others get it as a prop.
common_mistakes: Keeping a second useState for query inside SearchBox.

Code: return <input placeholder="Search breeds" value={query} onChange={e => setQuery(e.target.value)} />
